title: Base and prime editing delivery
bottleneck: Base and prime editors can correct mutations without double-strand breaks, safer than classic CRISPR, but the editor proteins are too large for single AAV vectors, requiring dual-vector systems with lower efficiency, and in vivo delivery to non-liver tissues remains unsolved.
why_it_blocks: These precise editors could address the majority of pathogenic point mutations, but only if they can be delivered efficiently to the affected tissue.
current_state: Dual-AAV prime editing recently achieved a first FDA approval for a rare deafness gene with Otarmeni, proving the concept in humans. Broad, efficient in vivo delivery is still ahead, and immune responses to vectors remain a constraint. The Otarmeni approval demonstrates that even oversized editors can reach patients via dual vectors, but efficiency and manufacturing complexity remain concerns. Tissue-targeted non-viral delivery could eventually bypass AAV's limits entirely.

sources.title: Otarmeni Approved by FDA as First Dual AAV Vector Gene Therapy for Rare Disease
